name: Nyx Whisperthread
equipment: Arcane focus (a cracked crystal that hums with psychic static)
A signet ring of a fictitious noble house
features: Sorcery Points (8): You have 8 sorcery points that you regain on a long rest. You can use sorcery points to fuel Metamagic options and Psionic Sorcery.
Font of Magic: You can convert unexpended spell slots into sorcery points (slot level = points gained), or spend sorcery points to create spell slots (2 points = 1st, 3 = 2nd, 5 = 3rd, 6 = 4th).
Metamagic: Subtle Spell (1 sorcery point): Cast a spell without any somatic or verbal components.

Metamagic: Twinned Spell (spell level in sorcery points, 1 min): When you cast a spell that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, spend sorcery points equal to the spell's level to target a second creature in range with the same spell.

Telepathic Speech: As a bonus action, you can establish telepathic communication with one creature you can see within 30 feet. The creature can understand you regardless of language, and it can respond telepathically. This link lasts for a number of minutes equal to your sorcerer level (8 minutes) and ends early if you are incapacitated, die, or use this feature on a different creature.

Psionic Sorcery: When you cast any Aberrant Mind spell (Dissonant Whispers, Arms of Hadar, Detect Thoughts, Calm Emotions, Hunger of Hadar, Sending, Evard's Black Tentacles, Summon Aberration), you can cast it by expending sorcery points equal to the spell's level instead of a spell slot, and if you do, the spell requires no verbal or somatic components.
Psychic Defenses: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.
Tiefling: Hellish Resistance: You have resistance to fire damage.

Tiefling: Infernal Legacy: You know the Thaumaturgy cantrip. Once you reach 3rd level, you can cast Hellish Rebuke as a 2nd-level spell once per long rest. Once you reach 5th level, you can cast Darkness once per long rest.

personality.traits: Nyx is a fast-talker, a natural performer who learned early that a convincing lie is worth more than a hard truth. She fills silence with quips, deflects sincerity with sarcasm, and keeps people at arm's length with charm so practiced it might as well be a cantrip. She reads a room the way a pickpocket reads a crowd — looking for leverage, exits, and the person most likely to cause trouble. But underneath the grifter's polish, there's a woman who hasn't slept well in months because the whispers in her head are getting louder, more coherent, and more insistent that she listen. She masks her fear with bravado and her vulnerability with jokes, and she'd rather set herself on fire than admit she needs help. Her telepathic abilities have made her paradoxically lonelier — she knows what people really think of her, and it's made genuine trust almost impossible.
personality.ideals: Freedom is the only currency that matters — freedom to move, to choose, to reinvent yourself whenever the old version stops working. Nyx has spent her entire life slipping out of constraints: bad situations, bad relationships, bad cities, bad identities. She believes that the moment you let someone else define who you are, you've already lost. But the Convergence is challenging this ideal in ways she didn't expect. The Astral Wardens speak of threads connecting all things, of responsibility to the fabric of reality itself, and some traitorous part of her wonders if running from connection is just another kind of prison. She's not ready to admit that yet. She still tells herself she's only helping because the alternatives — planar annihilation, the Confluence rewriting reality — are bad for business.
personality.bonds: Nyx's mother was a tiefling fortune-teller in the Rope Quarter of Anchorhold who could actually, genuinely see fragments of the future — a gift Nyx inherited and amplified a thousandfold when her Aberrant Mind powers awakened. Her mother disappeared three years ago, leaving behind only a cracked crystal focus and a journal of increasingly frantic visions about 'the threads unraveling.' Nyx carries both items and has been quietly searching for her mother across every plane the Convergence opens. She suspects her mother saw the Convergence coming and either went to stop it or was consumed by it. The other Threadwalkers don't know about this personal quest. Nyx also has an uneasy bond with the psychic presence that whispers at the edges of her mind — something that arrived with her powers, something that is not her quori spirit or a warlock patron, but something older and stranger that seems to live in the spaces between planes.
personality.flaws: Nyx is pathologically incapable of being straightforward when deception is an option. She lies about things she doesn't need to lie about — her age, her breakfast, whether she's cold — simply because honesty feels like exposure and exposure feels like danger. This compulsive dishonesty has cost her every meaningful relationship she's ever had, and she knows it, which makes her angry, which makes her lie more. She is also terrified of her own power in a way she refuses to examine. The Aberrant Mind abilities aren't just spells to her — they're evidence that something fundamentally alien has taken up residence in her psyche, and every time she uses Psionic Sorcery, she feels it settle in a little deeper. She pushes her powers harder than she should, daring the thing inside her to show itself, because the waiting and wondering is worse than any confrontation could be. She also has a weakness for gambling — the weighted dice are a safety net she can't quite bring herself to throw away.

appearance: Nyx stands about five and a half feet tall with the lean, wiry build of someone who has spent more of her life running from things than standing to face them. Her skin is a deep lavender-gray, smooth and cool to the touch, with a faint luminescent quality that becomes visible in dim light — a side effect of her Aberrant Mind awakening that she hasn't been able to suppress. Her horns are slender and swept back, curving elegantly from her temples to just past the crown of her head, and she's taken to wrapping them in thin silver wire that she claims is decorative but actually helps ground the psychic static that builds up during extended telepathic use. Her eyes are her most striking feature: they were solid amber before her powers awakened, but now they shift — the irises fracture and reform like kaleidoscopes when she's channeling psionic energy, and in moments of extreme psychic exertion, her pupils dilate into impossible geometric shapes that hurt to look at directly. Her hair is ink-black, cut asymmetrically short on one side and falling past her jaw on the other, and it moves slightly in nonexistent breezes when she's concentrating. Her tail is long and prehensile, ending in a spade-shaped tip that she uses expressively — it betrays emotions her face is too well-trained to show. She dresses in dark, well-tailored clothes that look expensive but are actually clever fakes — a charlatan's habit she can't break — with a long coat whose interior pockets contain an improbable number of useful items. Her cracked crystal arcane focus hangs on a leather cord around her neck, pulsing with a faint violet light that syncs with her heartbeat. Faint, web-like patterns of silver occasionally trace across her forearms and hands when she casts psionic spells, like circuit diagrams drawn in starlight, fading within seconds.
backstory:
Nyx was born in the Rope Quarter of a sprawling port city to a tiefling fortune-teller named Vex Whisperthread and a father she never met. Her mother's fortune-telling was the real thing — fragmentary, unreliable, but genuine precognition — and it kept them fed, housed, and one step ahead of the various people who wanted to exploit or silence a tiefling seer. Nyx grew up learning that the truth was a commodity to be traded carefully, that appearances were armor, and that the best defense against a hostile world was being someone else entirely. She took to the charlatan's trade naturally, running cons and confidence schemes from the age of fourteen, using her mother's genuine gift as cover for her own manufactured predictions.

By twenty, Nyx was one of the most successful grifters in the city — not because she was the cleverest, but because she was the most adaptable. She could read a mark's desires in seconds and become whatever they needed her to be. She ran long cons on merchants, short cons on sailors, and once impersonated a minor noble for three months to gain access to a library of forbidden texts her mother wanted to consult. She was good at what she did, and she was miserable in the way that people who are very good at pretending to be someone else often are — because the person underneath the masks had become increasingly difficult to locate.

Everything changed eighteen months ago. Nyx was in the middle of a con — impersonating an astrologer at a wealthy merchant's party — when reality hiccupped. A micro-zone of the Convergence opened in the merchant's parlor, a hairline crack in the fabric of the planes that lasted less than three seconds. But in those three seconds, something reached through and touched Nyx's mind. Her latent sorcerous bloodline, dormant her entire life, detonated. Every glass in the room shattered. Every person within thirty feet heard her thoughts — her real thoughts, the terrified internal monologue of a con artist whose mask had just been ripped away. She levitated six inches off the ground, her eyes went fractal, and a voice that was not hers spoke through her mouth in Deep Speech: 'The threads are unraveling. She knew. She tried to warn you.'

Nyx fled the city that night. Her mother had disappeared two months prior, leaving behind her cracked crystal focus and a journal filled with increasingly desperate notes about planar convergence, thread-mathematics, and something called 'the Confluence.' Nyx had dismissed the journal as evidence of her mother's declining mental health. Now she read it with new eyes and growing horror.

The Astral Wardens found her three weeks later, wandering the Silver Wastes in a state of psychic overload, her newly awakened powers broadcasting her thoughts to everything within a hundred feet. The githzerai monks recognized what she was — an Aberrant Mind sorcerer whose powers had been triggered by direct contact with the Convergence — and offered her training, stability, and answers. She accepted, though she told them she was only staying until she found her mother. That was a year ago. She's still here, her powers growing stronger and stranger, the whispers in her mind growing more coherent, and the silver compass shard she was given humming in harmony with the thing inside her head in a way that she finds deeply unsettling and absolutely refuses to discuss.
